analysis.title: GS Basics: Resilient. Inflation Persistent. Home Drones (Rich Privorotsky, 11 Nov 2026)
key_insights: October CPI came in hot across the board: headline +0.4%, core +0.3%, with strength extending beyond energy into medical services, insurance and other categories. The note argues this is hard to dismiss as energy pass-through and that underlying inflation is sticky.
Combined with hawkish comments from Waller and Logan, markets now price a December hike plus some optionality of 50bp, and further tightening into 2027. The curve is bear flattening.
SPX barely fell yesterday and futures are recovering this morning. The note says AI sentiment appears to be improving and supports the core engines of the market.
VIX briefly traded into the 20s on the CPI print but finished below 20. The note says positioning may now be doing more to support the tape than the macro is doing to undermine it.

Nets are historically low, gross has been cut and investors are heavily hedged. The note calls positioning a tailwind and the Fed a headwind, and expects the volatility premium to keep decaying absent fresh negative information.

Neocloud commentary overnight was broadly supportive. Data center capacity constraints remain the primary operational bottleneck and compute utilization across major providers remains elevated. Market focus is on hardware delivery and developer coding workflows, while edge and enterprise autonomous integrations are at earlier stages.

On oil, Rubio said after the G7 meetings in Paris that the administration favors sustained economic pressure and the naval blockade over an immediate return to major combat operations. Per wire reports, Qatari mediators are working within an estimated two-week diplomatic window, with parameters unconfirmed.

The key tactical question is whether Tehran tolerates the blockade status quo over the coming days. Brent has bounced off yesterday's lows but directional conviction is low. If Brent consolidates near $90 with collapsing realized volatility, the note expects equities to look through headline noise.

Rates are a headwind but the market has built a cushion from the prior rally. Yields need another leg higher before they become a material problem for equities, since the rate of change is what matters.

Credit is the area to watch, with high yield spreads chopping sideways. The note flags reflexivity with energy: higher oil, stickier inflation, a more hawkish Fed. It asks whether the Fed is reacting to energy effects already in the past or to something more persistent.
US Veterans Day today: bond market closed, equities open. The desk is watching the neoclouds and the next move in energy.
Side note: Amazon's Ring unveiled a flying drone and a robot to patrol homes and businesses.
